summary: Edge proxy retry loop causes SSE stream freeze during long chat sessions
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated streaming chat sessions (SSE) that begin normally but freeze mid-generation after ~30-120s. The client observes no final event and connection remains open; eventually client-side times out. This appears correlated with bursts of 502/504 responses from an edge proxy in front of Redwood’s API and aggressive automatic retries by that proxy.

Impact: Several paid customers on Dedicated capacity experienced degraded UX for long multi-turn chats. Affected customers reported multiple sessions where partial output is delivered then stalls; some sessions recovered after forcing a client reconnect, others required server-side fix. No data exfiltration suspected.

Why this ticket: Customer asked for root cause, mitigation, and permanent fix. Ticket captures investigation and resolution plan.
impact: Partial streaming output for long chats, client-visible stalls, increased support load. Customer reported ~12 impacted sessions across two accounts in the last 48h.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a dedicated customer account with reserved capacity and open a long multi-turn SSE chat (>1k tokens).
2) Trigger a response that takes >30s to stream (complex prompt + external tool calls simulated),
3) During streaming, cause transient edge-proxy resource pressure (simulate burst of concurrent requests or apply artificial 502s),
4) Observe that SSE stream delivers some chunks then pauses indefinitely; client stays connected and no final event is emitted.
logs: 2026-03-09T14:22:11Z request_id=abc123 retried by proxy (X-Retry: 1) -> new connection request_id=abc123-1, server accepted but stream eventually unblocks on worker but client sees no final chunk
2026-03-09T14:22:35Z serving-runtime: kv-cache-lock wait 240ms prior to emit chunk seq=12
2026-03-09T14:22:58Z connection remaining open, no further chunks; client-side heartbeat OK until client timeout at 2026-03-09T14:24:10Z
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: serving runtime kernel swap or kv-cache eviction causing mid-stream stall. Logs show short cache waits but not long enough to explain full freeze.

Observed correlation: edge-proxy returned 502 for the original upstream connection then attempted an automatic retry. Proxy attaches X-Retry header and opens a new downstream connection with same request semantics.

Race condition found: server-side streaming handler expects a single long-lived connection per request_id. When a proxy retry opens a second connection carrying same idempotency markers, the server forks a second handler for the same logical stream but continues to keep the first stream in a semi-finalized state. Streaming chunks are interleaved; client receives first handler's output then stalls because jittered backpressure and connection pinning hold remaining tokens in the other handler.
Edge-proxy setup: retries for non-idempotent POSTs were enabled for a short window after recent config change to mitigate transient network errors. This is unsafe for streaming endpoints.
Reproducible locally by turning on proxy retry policy against the streaming endpoint; disabling retry restores correct behavior.
comments: Support (Aisha Romero) 2026-03-10: Customer reported multiple sessions freezing mid-stream. Attached client logs and sample request ids. Escalating to SRE.

SRE (Liam Chen) 2026-03-10: Running live capture on edge-proxy-3; saw intermittent 502s followed by proxy-level retries for streaming POSTs. Hypothesis: proxy retries are causing duplicate upstream streams.
Customer (Elena, SynthDesk) 2026-03-11: We see similar behaviour in eu-west. Workaround of forcing client reconnect temporarily helps but hurts UX.
SRE (Liam Chen) 2026-03-11: Applied emergency config rollback on edge-proxy to disable automatic retries for POST /v1/stream endpoints. Monitoring for 6h.
Support (Aisha Romero) 2026-03-12: Customer confirmed significant reduction in incidents after rollback. Requesting a permanent fix and PR for config hardening.

Engineering (Diego Patel) 2026-03-12: Prepared PR to make serving-runtime reject duplicate retry connections for streaming sessions and to use explicit retry token negotiation when safe (https PR linked).
resolution: Mitigation applied: disabled automatic retries for POST streaming endpoints at edge proxy and rolled out server-side guard to reject duplicate in-flight retry connections for the same request id. Permanent fix planned: proxy config hardening + serving-runtime PR to unify idempotency negotiation.
resolution_notes: Rollback completed 2026-03-11 22:40Z. Serving-runtime change merged to trunk and will be rolled to prod in next canary window (2026-03-14). Customer SynthDesk verified decreased incident frequency and accepted interim mitigation. Follow-up: add automated test simulating proxy retries against streaming endpoints and update runbook.
next_steps: 1) Deploy serving-runtime PR to canary and monitor streaming metrics (rollout 2026-03-14).
2) Add proxy rule to explicitly never retry streaming POSTs and add a unit test for config (owner: edge-proxy team).
3) Update incident runbook and add a detection alert for X-Retry headers appearing on active live streams.
4) Customer outreach: schedule postmortem call with SynthDesk to review timeline and corrective actions.
